families.title: Operationalize the desired outcome
families.method: Translate the request into an observable result and state how the result will be recognized.
families.boundary: Do not confuse a convenient proxy with the actual outcome.

families.title: Separate outcome from deliverable
families.method: Record the change sought separately from the artifact or action proposed to produce it.
families.boundary: A deliverable can be completed without producing the intended outcome.

families.title: Define the decision boundary
families.method: State which choices are inside the current decision and which are fixed or delegated.
families.boundary: Reopen a fixed boundary only when evidence shows the premise is invalid.

families.title: Build an assumptions register
families.method: Write each assumption as a testable proposition and attach an owner or evidence source when possible.
families.boundary: An assumption is not a fact merely because a plan depends on it.

families.title: Record negative requirements
families.method: List outcomes, states, or side effects that must not occur.
families.boundary: Check that a negative requirement does not contradict a mandatory objective.

families.title: Identify affected stakeholders
families.method: List parties who use, supply, approve, maintain, or bear consequences of the result.
families.boundary: Do not treat the loudest stakeholder as the complete stakeholder set.

families.title: Establish acceptance criteria
families.method: Turn success into observable conditions that can be checked independently.
families.boundary: Avoid criteria that merely repeat the proposed solution.

families.title: Create a shared term glossary
families.method: Define ambiguous task terms before comparing claims that use them.
families.boundary: Preserve competing definitions when the field has no single agreed meaning.

families.title: Set an explicit scope perimeter
families.method: Name included cases, excluded cases, and the reason for each boundary.
families.boundary: Do not silently generalize conclusions beyond the declared perimeter.

families.title: Capture the baseline state
families.method: Describe the current state using the same measures intended for later comparison.
families.boundary: Do not compare a measured future state with an unmeasured baseline.

families.title: Separate needs from preferences
families.method: Classify each request as essential, desirable, optional, or prohibited.
families.boundary: A preference can become mandatory only when an authorized decision-maker says so.

families.title: Specify the unit of analysis
families.method: State whether the reasoning concerns an individual, instance, group, system, event, or time period.
families.boundary: Do not switch units midway through an argument.

families.title: Bound the time horizon
families.method: Specify when effects begin, how long they are assessed, and what counts as the endpoint.
families.boundary: Do not omit long-term effects merely because they fall outside the immediate task.

families.title: Identify the responsible decision owner
families.method: Record who has authority to choose, accept residual risk, or request more evidence.
families.boundary: Do not infer authority from participation or technical expertise.

families.title: Turn vague adjectives into tests
families.method: Replace words such as fast, robust, simple, or safe with measurable or inspectable criteria.
families.boundary: When measurement is impossible, state the proxy and its limitation.

families.title: Record the reason for the task
families.method: State the condition that makes the task necessary now.
families.boundary: Do not confuse the stated motivation with an independently established cause.

families.title: Distinguish current state from target state
families.method: Describe the starting condition and desired condition in separate fields.
families.boundary: Do not present a desired state as though it already exists.

families.title: Define completion and handoff
families.method: Specify the evidence needed to close the task and who receives the result.
families.boundary: A finished analysis is not automatically an accepted implementation.

families.title: Capture environmental constraints
families.method: List legal, physical, social, technical, and operational constraints that affect feasibility.
families.boundary: Mark constraints that are merely assumed and verify them where consequential.

families.title: Write a decision brief before solving
families.method: Summarize the question, objective, scope, constraints, and required decision in a compact brief.
families.boundary: Revise the brief when new evidence changes the problem rather than hiding the change.

families.title: Choose the model boundary
families.method: Identify entities, processes, and external influences included in the model.
families.boundary: A boundary is a modeling choice, not proof that excluded influences do not matter.

families.title: Distinguish state from parameter
families.method: Separate quantities that change during the process from settings treated as fixed for the analysis.
families.boundary: Reclassify a parameter when evidence shows it varies on the relevant timescale.

families.title: Choose a fit-for-purpose abstraction
families.method: Retain details that affect the decision and omit details that do not change the result materially.
families.boundary: Do not simplify away a known failure mode or safety constraint.

families.title: Represent the process as stages
families.method: Describe major stages and the outputs passed between them.
families.boundary: Do not imply a strict sequence when stages can occur concurrently.

families.title: Mark interfaces explicitly
families.method: Specify what each component receives, produces, and assumes about adjacent components.
families.boundary: An interface description is incomplete if units, timing, or error behavior are omitted.

families.title: Separate mechanism from correlation
families.method: Represent the proposed mechanism separately from observed co-variation.
families.boundary: A plausible mechanism does not by itself establish that the mechanism operated.

families.title: Track state transitions
families.method: Define the conditions that move a system from one state to another.
families.boundary: Include invalid, terminal, and recovery states when they are possible.

families.title: Use a causal map cautiously
families.method: Draw candidate influence links and label each as observed, assumed, or experimentally supported.
families.boundary: Do not read a drawn arrow as proof of causation.

families.title: Expose hidden intermediate variables
families.method: Ask which unobserved stages could connect the input to the claimed outcome.
families.boundary: Do not invent an intermediate variable solely to rescue a preferred explanation.

families.title: Choose model granularity deliberately
families.method: Select the smallest level of detail that preserves distinctions relevant to the task.
families.boundary: Increase detail when aggregated values hide subgroup behavior or boundary failures.

families.title: Represent feedback paths
families.method: Identify outputs that feed back into earlier decisions or system states.
families.boundary: Include delay and sign of influence; feedback is not always stabilizing.

families.title: Mark external dependencies
families.method: List conditions controlled outside the modeled system that can affect its behavior.
families.boundary: Do not assume an external dependency is guaranteed or under local control.

families.title: Separate observable from latent quantities
families.method: Label directly measured variables and inferred constructs distinctly.
families.boundary: State how a latent quantity is operationalized and what that proxy misses.

families.title: Build a dependency map
families.method: Connect prerequisite conditions to the tasks or results that rely on them.
families.boundary: A dependency link should have a concrete reason, not merely temporal proximity.

families.title: Identify conservation or accounting boundaries
families.method: Define what flows into, out of, and remains within the modeled scope.
families.boundary: Check for untracked transfers before interpreting a residual as unexplained loss.

families.title: Represent multiple levels
families.method: Separate local behavior, subsystem behavior, and whole-system outcomes.
families.boundary: Do not assume local improvements sum to a system-level improvement.

families.title: Separate policy from mechanism
families.method: Represent chosen rules or controls apart from the process they influence.
families.boundary: A policy description is not evidence that the policy is followed.

families.title: Expose model assumptions in the diagram
families.method: Attach assumptions to the elements or links that rely on them.
families.boundary: Do not hide assumptions in labels that appear to be observed data.

families.title: Select a proxy with a validity argument
families.method: Explain why the proxy tracks the target and under what conditions it can fail.
families.boundary: Do not use ease of measurement as the only reason for proxy selection.

families.title: Define model-use limits
families.method: State which questions the model can answer and which it cannot.
families.boundary: Do not transfer a model beyond its tested scope without a new validation step.

families.title: Construct a milestone ladder
families.method: Break the objective into observable intermediate milestones with completion evidence.
families.boundary: Milestones should represent meaningful progress rather than arbitrary calendar divisions.

families.title: Identify the critical dependency chain
families.method: Find the longest sequence of dependent tasks that constrains completion.
families.boundary: Recalculate when dependencies or task durations change.

families.title: Reserve a contingency path
families.method: Define a viable alternative for the most consequential plan failure.
families.boundary: A contingency that requires the same failed resource is not independent.

families.title: Prioritize by expected value of effort
families.method: Rank work by likely contribution to the objective relative to effort and risk.
families.boundary: Do not treat uncertain estimates as precise rankings.

families.title: Use staged commitment
families.method: Delay costly irreversible commitments until the information needed to justify them is available.
families.boundary: Do not delay low-cost reversible actions that would safely produce useful information.

families.title: Set a search frontier
families.method: Maintain explicit candidate next actions and the reason each remains worth exploring.
families.boundary: Remove actions whose prerequisites have failed or whose expected value is dominated.

families.title: Allocate effort to the bottleneck
families.method: Direct the next unit of effort toward the constraint limiting overall progress.
families.boundary: Verify that the apparent bottleneck is not merely the most visible problem.

families.title: Plan around resource peaks
families.method: Schedule tasks so simultaneous demands do not exceed available capacity.
families.boundary: Account for setup, recovery, and coordination time as resource use.

families.title: Use a staged fallback
families.method: Define a simpler acceptable outcome if the full plan becomes infeasible.
families.boundary: Do not silently redefine the original success criterion after failure.

families.title: Make the plan observable
families.method: Attach a measurable progress signal to each major step.
families.boundary: A progress signal should not reward activity that does not advance the objective.

families.title: Separate exploration from execution
families.method: Allocate explicit time or budget to learn and a separate budget to deliver.
families.boundary: Do not allow open-ended exploration to consume the delivery reserve.

families.title: Choose the next informative action
families.method: Prefer a safe action that reduces a decision-relevant uncertainty.
families.boundary: Information has little value when it cannot change the next decision.

families.title: Batch independent work
families.method: Group tasks that share setup costs when their outcomes do not depend on order.
families.boundary: Do not batch tasks when early results should change later choices.

families.title: Preserve option value
families.method: Keep feasible alternatives open when the cost of waiting is low and new information is expected.
families.boundary: Do not preserve options whose carrying cost exceeds their likely future value.

families.title: Schedule prerequisite checks first
families.method: Verify high-impact prerequisites before committing downstream work.
families.boundary: Use proportionate checks; do not test trivial prerequisites more heavily than the risk warrants.

families.title: Define a revisit trigger
families.method: Specify what evidence or event would justify reopening the current plan.
families.boundary: Avoid both constant reconsideration and rigid refusal to adapt.

families.title: Control plan complexity
families.method: Prefer the simplest plan that satisfies the objective and constraints.
families.boundary: A short plan is not simpler when it hides coordination or recovery work.

families.title: Sequence by risk exposure
families.method: Complete low-cost checks that can prevent high-cost downstream mistakes early.
families.boundary: Do not postpone mandatory safety or compliance checks for schedule convenience.

families.title: Plan a clean stopping point
families.method: Define a state in which work can pause without losing essential context.
families.boundary: Record pending assumptions, open decisions, and restart conditions.

families.title: Use a decision checkpoint
families.method: Pause at named milestones to compare actual state with the plan before proceeding.
families.boundary: A checkpoint must be allowed to change or stop the plan.

families.title: Trace each claim to its evidence
families.method: Attach each material claim to the observation, document, measurement, or derivation that supports it.
families.boundary: A nearby citation is not sufficient if it supports a different claim.

families.title: Check source proximity
families.method: Prefer evidence produced by the actor, instrument, or event directly relevant to the claim.
families.boundary: Primary status does not remove the need to assess methods and bias.

families.title: Record evidence collection conditions
families.method: Capture when, where, how, and by whom the evidence was obtained.
families.boundary: Missing collection context limits reproducibility and interpretation.

families.title: Separate evidence quantity from quality
families.method: Assess relevance, method, independence, and bias separately from the number of sources.
families.boundary: Many copied sources do not create independent corroboration.

families.title: Check source independence
families.method: Determine whether apparently separate reports rely on the same original dataset or authority.
families.boundary: Shared upstream evidence should not be counted as multiple confirmations.

families.title: Assess sample coverage
families.method: Compare who or what was observed with the population the conclusion concerns.
families.boundary: A large but systematically selected sample can remain unrepresentative.

families.title: Inspect missing-data patterns
families.method: Record which observations are absent and whether absence is related to the outcome.
families.boundary: Do not assume missing observations are random without support.

families.title: Check measurement validity
families.method: Explain why the instrument or proxy measures the property under discussion.
families.boundary: Precision of a reading does not establish validity of the construct.

families.title: Separate direct observation from report
families.method: Label what was observed firsthand and what was relayed by another party.
families.boundary: Do not silently upgrade a report into a direct observation.

families.title: Check temporal relevance
families.method: Compare the evidence date with the time period of the claim.
families.boundary: Older evidence may remain useful for stable principles but not for changing conditions.

families.title: Inspect selection mechanisms
families.method: Ask how cases entered the observed dataset and which cases were excluded.
families.boundary: Conclusions may not generalize when inclusion depends on the outcome.

families.title: Check denominator completeness
families.method: Identify the full set of opportunities, cases, or exposures behind a reported rate.
families.boundary: A numerator without a reliable denominator cannot establish the rate.

families.title: Preserve contradictory observations
families.method: Store material evidence that does not fit the leading account.
families.boundary: Do not discard a contradiction merely because it is inconvenient.

families.title: Assess evidence relevance
families.method: Map each item to the exact question it can answer.
families.boundary: Evidence about a related population or outcome may not transfer.

families.title: Check replication conditions
families.method: Compare whether repeated observations used meaningfully independent settings or methods.
families.boundary: Repeated use of one shared pipeline is not independent reproduction.

families.title: Inspect reporting incentives
families.method: Consider whether data collection or presentation creates incentives to omit unfavorable results.
families.boundary: An incentive concern is a reason to inspect methods, not automatic proof of misconduct.

families.title: Check version and provenance
families.method: Record dataset, document, instrument, and method versions.
families.boundary: Do not combine incompatible versions without documenting the change.

families.title: Separate absence of evidence from evidence of absence
families.method: Ask whether the observation process had enough power or coverage to detect the event.
families.boundary: A failed detection is informative only relative to detection capability.

families.title: Use triangulation across methods
families.method: Compare evidence gathered through methods with different failure modes.
families.boundary: Agreement among methods is weak when they share the same hidden assumption.

families.title: Create an evidence ledger
families.method: Maintain claim, support, limitation, source, date, and review status in one traceable record.
families.boundary: A ledger organizes evidence; it does not itself validate the evidence.

families.title: Write a mechanism chain
families.method: Describe the intermediate steps connecting a proposed input to the observed outcome.
families.boundary: Do not treat a gap in the chain as established merely because the endpoints correlate.

families.title: Distinguish necessary from sufficient conditions
families.method: State whether a condition must be present, can produce the result alone, or merely contributes.
families.boundary: Avoid using these terms without checking alternative routes and exceptions.

families.title: Identify enabling conditions
families.method: List conditions that allow a mechanism to operate even if they do not cause the outcome alone.
families.boundary: Do not confuse an enabling condition with the direct driver.

families.title: Identify blocking conditions
families.method: List circumstances that prevent a proposed mechanism from reaching its outcome.
families.boundary: A failed mechanism under a blocker does not always refute the mechanism generally.

families.title: Compare mechanism predictions
families.method: Derive an observable implication from each proposed mechanism before checking the data.
families.boundary: Avoid post-hoc predictions that could fit almost any outcome.

families.title: Explain intermediate timing
families.method: Specify the expected order and delay of mechanism stages.
families.boundary: A timing mismatch is evidence against a mechanism only when timing assumptions are justified.

families.title: Track mechanism scope
families.method: State the settings or populations in which the mechanism is expected to operate.
families.boundary: Do not universalize a context-dependent mechanism.

families.title: Separate actor intent from system effect
families.method: Analyze what an actor intended and what the system actually produced as different claims.
families.boundary: Observed impact does not prove intent.

families.title: Distinguish trigger from underlying condition
families.method: Separate the immediate event that initiates a process from persistent conditions that make it possible.
families.boundary: Removing a trigger may not eliminate the underlying vulnerability.

families.title: Map multiple pathways
families.method: Represent alternative paths that can lead to the same observed result.
families.boundary: Do not assume a single pathway when evidence allows multiple routes.

families.title: Inspect mechanism bottlenecks
families.method: Identify the stage where the proposed process is most likely to stop or weaken.
families.boundary: Do not attribute all failures to the most visible stage.

families.title: Test mechanism reversibility
families.method: Ask whether reversing the proposed cause should reverse the effect and under what lag.
families.boundary: Irreversible accumulation or hysteresis can invalidate a simple reversal expectation.

families.title: Separate proximate and distal explanations
families.method: Distinguish immediate process explanations from background or structural explanations.
families.boundary: Do not treat explanations at different levels as mutually exclusive by default.

families.title: State the mechanism counterfactual
families.method: Describe what the mechanism predicts would happen if a key component were absent.
families.boundary: A counterfactual prediction depends on what else is held fixed.

families.title: Look for mediator evidence
families.method: Identify observations that should occur between the intervention and final outcome.
families.boundary: A mediator association alone does not establish the complete pathway.

families.title: Check mechanism consistency
families.method: Verify that the proposed stages do not contradict known constraints or each other.
families.boundary: An internally coherent story can still be empirically false.

families.title: Distinguish mechanism change from parameter change
families.method: Ask whether the process itself changed or only its speed, scale, or threshold.
families.boundary: Use evidence about process structure rather than labels alone.

families.title: Track unintended pathways
families.method: List plausible routes by which an action could create effects outside its intended channel.
families.boundary: Include beneficial and harmful side effects.

families.title: Explain failure at the right level
families.method: Locate whether failure arose in assumptions, mechanism, implementation, or measurement.
families.boundary: Do not change the theory to explain an implementation error without evidence.

families.title: Produce a minimal causal narrative
families.method: Explain the smallest set of supported steps sufficient to account for the observation.
families.boundary: Minimality is not a reason to omit known competing pathways.

families.title: Generate a genuine option set
families.method: Create materially different ways to meet the same objective, including a do-minimum or status-quo option where relevant.
families.boundary: Do not compare a preferred option with deliberately weak alternatives.

families.title: Apply hard constraints before scoring
families.method: Remove options that violate non-negotiable requirements before comparing preferences.
families.boundary: Record the violated constraint and do not hide it inside a low score.

families.title: Use common comparison criteria
families.method: Evaluate alternatives against the same defined criteria and evidence standard.
families.boundary: Add criteria only when they are relevant to the decision and applied consistently.

families.title: Expose trade-offs explicitly
families.method: State what each option gains and sacrifices rather than collapsing all dimensions into one label.
families.boundary: Do not invent weights where decision authority has not supplied them.

families.title: Identify dominated alternatives
families.method: Remove an option only when another is at least as good on all relevant dimensions and better on one.
families.boundary: Check that criteria and uncertainty ranges are comparable before dominance claims.

families.title: Separate value judgments from measurements
families.method: Label empirical estimates separately from chosen weights or preferences.
families.boundary: A numeric score does not make a value judgment objective.

families.title: Include opportunity cost
families.method: Record the best alternative use of resources displaced by the chosen option.
families.boundary: Do not count the same foregone benefit twice.

families.title: Evaluate reversibility
families.method: Estimate the cost, delay, and feasibility of undoing each option.
families.boundary: Do not treat a theoretically reversible decision as practically reversible if switching costs are high.

families.title: Use a decision threshold
families.method: Specify the evidence or performance level required to choose, defer, or reject.
families.boundary: Set the threshold before seeing the final result when hindsight bias is a concern.

families.title: Run a switching-value check
families.method: Find how far a key assumption must change before the preferred option changes.
families.boundary: A switching value is conditional on the model and other assumptions.

families.title: Separate expected value from risk tolerance
families.method: Report average projected outcomes and downside exposure separately.
families.boundary: Do not assume the decision-maker is risk neutral.

families.title: Include distributional effects
families.method: Record which groups receive benefits, costs, risks, or burdens.
families.boundary: An aggregate gain can conceal concentrated harm.

families.title: Assess option interactions
families.method: Check whether combining options creates synergies, conflicts, or duplicated costs.
families.boundary: Do not add standalone benefits when the options interact.

families.title: Use a staged decision
families.method: Split a large choice into smaller decisions that can incorporate new information.
families.boundary: Ensure early stages do not lock in the full cost unintentionally.

families.title: Compare against business as usual
families.method: Estimate what is likely under no new intervention to create a reference case.
families.boundary: The baseline is not necessarily zero cost or zero change.

families.title: Document the selection rationale
families.method: Record criteria, alternatives, assumptions, results, and reasons for the final choice.
families.boundary: Do not record only the recommendation; retain the rejected options and uncertainty.

families.title: Assess unintended incentives
families.method: Ask how each option changes incentives and what behavior it may reward.
families.boundary: Do not assume stated policy intent determines actual behavior.

families.title: Use proportionate analysis depth
families.method: Match analytical effort to decision cost, reversibility, and potential harm.
families.boundary: High stakes or irreversible outcomes require stronger evidence and review.

families.title: Preserve a no-action option
families.method: Evaluate whether acting now is better than waiting or doing nothing.
families.boundary: Do not use no-action as a straw option; estimate its consequences fairly.

families.title: State the decision owner and review date
families.method: Record who accepts the choice and when its assumptions should be revisited.
families.boundary: A review date does not imply that the decision is automatically invalid then.

families.title: Define the learning question
families.method: State which uncertainty the test is intended to reduce and what decision depends on it.
families.boundary: Do not run a test whose result cannot change any action.

families.title: Pilot before scaling
families.method: Test the procedure on a limited, representative scope before broad deployment.
families.boundary: A small pilot may miss rare failures; state what it cannot establish.

families.title: Change one controllable factor at a time
families.method: When isolating a mechanism, keep other controllable conditions stable while varying the target factor.
families.boundary: This is not appropriate when interactions are the main object of study.

families.title: Predefine outcome measures
families.method: Choose the outcome and measurement method before observing test results.
families.boundary: Do not select the success metric after seeing which one favors the result.

families.title: Include a comparison condition
families.method: Use a suitable baseline or comparison group when the question requires separating change from background variation.
families.boundary: The comparison must be sufficiently similar for the inference being made.

families.title: Repeat under changed conditions
families.method: Test whether a result persists across relevant environments, users, or operating conditions.
families.boundary: Do not call repeated runs independent when they share the same failure source.

families.title: Use a negative control
families.method: Include a condition in which the proposed effect should not appear.
families.boundary: A failed negative control may invalidate interpretation of the positive result.

families.title: Use a positive control
families.method: Include a condition expected to produce a known response when the setup is functioning.
families.boundary: A positive control does not show that the target hypothesis is correct.

families.title: Separate exploratory from confirmatory tests
families.method: Label tests used to discover patterns separately from tests designed to confirm a prespecified prediction.
families.boundary: Do not treat a pattern found during exploration as independently confirmed.

families.title: Record failed trials
families.method: Store unexpected and unsuccessful outcomes with the same care as successful ones.
families.boundary: Do not remove failed runs without a documented exclusion reason.

families.title: Check measurement repeatability
families.method: Repeat the same measurement under comparable conditions to assess measurement variation.
families.boundary: Repeatability does not establish accuracy.

families.title: Vary boundary conditions
families.method: Test near the limits of the stated operating range.
families.boundary: Do not extrapolate beyond tested boundaries without a model and validation.

families.title: Use an ablation test
families.method: Remove one component at a time to determine whether it contributes to the result.
families.boundary: Ablation can change interactions; interpret removal effects in context.

families.title: Test an alternative implementation
families.method: Use a distinct implementation or method to check whether the result depends on one pipeline.
families.boundary: Different implementations can still share the same conceptual error.

families.title: Measure side effects
families.method: Record outcomes that could worsen while the primary metric improves.
families.boundary: A narrow success metric can conceal harm elsewhere.

families.title: Choose an informative sample
families.method: Select cases that expose the decision-relevant range of conditions.
families.boundary: Do not confuse a stress sample with a representative prevalence sample.

families.title: Define a replication target
families.method: Specify which finding, environment, and method another run must reproduce.
families.boundary: A vague request to reproduce the result is not an executable replication plan.

families.title: Preserve test configuration
families.method: Record software, inputs, instruments, parameters, and environment for each run.
families.boundary: A result without configuration cannot be reliably compared.

families.title: Use a staged rollout
families.method: Increase exposure gradually while monitoring predefined failure indicators.
families.boundary: Stop or roll back when a safety or reliability threshold is crossed.

families.title: Close the learning loop
families.method: Compare predicted and observed outcomes and update the relevant model or procedure.
families.boundary: Do not update a rule from one atypical observation without assessing its cause.

families.title: Compare expected and observed behavior
families.method: Write the expected output for the current inputs and compare it with the actual output.
families.boundary: The expectation itself must be checked before treating the difference as a fault.

families.title: Localize the first divergence
families.method: Trace the process until the earliest point where observed behavior departs from expectation.
families.boundary: The first visible error may be downstream of the actual fault.

families.title: Isolate one subsystem
families.method: Hold unaffected components constant while testing the suspected component.
families.boundary: Isolation is invalid when the suspected behavior depends on cross-component interaction.

families.title: Reproduce the failure minimally
families.method: Reduce a failure to the smallest input and sequence that still triggers it.
families.boundary: Do not remove a condition that is necessary to reproduce the failure.

families.title: Classify failure mode
families.method: Label the symptom as missing output, wrong output, timing error, resource exhaustion, or unsafe state.
families.boundary: A symptom category is a starting point, not a root-cause conclusion.

families.title: Check recent changes first
families.method: Compare the working and failing configurations for recent changes in code, process, data, or environment.
families.boundary: Temporal proximity alone does not prove a change caused the failure.

families.title: Inspect boundary behavior
families.method: Test empty, minimum, maximum, malformed, and transition inputs relevant to the system.
families.boundary: Choose boundaries from the specification rather than arbitrary extremes.

families.title: Separate intermittent from deterministic failure
families.method: Repeat under controlled conditions and record whether the same inputs yield the same outcome.
families.boundary: Do not call a failure random until uncontrolled variables are considered.

families.title: Check resource exhaustion
families.method: Measure resource use over time and compare it with capacity and expected load.
families.boundary: A resource warning is not a root cause unless it aligns with the failure.

families.title: Trace error propagation
families.method: Follow how an initial fault changes downstream state and outputs.
families.boundary: Do not mistake the largest downstream symptom for the origin.

families.title: Use a fault tree
families.method: Start from the undesired event and enumerate combinations of conditions that could produce it.
families.boundary: A fault tree is incomplete until common-cause and dependency effects are considered.

families.title: Check configuration drift
families.method: Compare deployed settings with the reviewed or intended configuration.
families.boundary: A configuration difference matters only if it affects the relevant behavior.

families.title: Distinguish symptom suppression from repair
families.method: Determine whether a change removes the cause or merely hides its visible effect.
families.boundary: A workaround must remain labelled as a workaround until root cause is addressed.

families.title: Test recovery behavior
families.method: After inducing a safe failure, observe whether the system returns to a valid state.
families.boundary: Do not test recovery in production when the induced fault could cause harm.

families.title: Verify diagnostic instrumentation
families.method: Confirm that logs, sensors, or traces faithfully represent the event being diagnosed.
families.boundary: An instrument fault can mimic a system fault.

families.title: Check for multiple simultaneous faults
families.method: Test whether one repair leaves another independent symptom unresolved.
families.boundary: Do not force all observations into one root cause without evidence.

families.title: Compare failure and success cases
families.method: Identify conditions that differ between otherwise comparable successful and failed runs.
families.boundary: A difference is a lead for testing, not proof of causal relevance.

families.title: Use a rollback test
families.method: Restore a known-good version or configuration in a controlled environment to assess whether behavior returns.
families.boundary: Rollback may be confounded by persistent state or external changes.

families.title: Validate the repair against regression cases
families.method: Re-run the original failure and nearby behaviors after applying a fix.
families.boundary: A fix is incomplete if it resolves one case by breaking a required adjacent case.

families.title: Write a root-cause record
families.method: Document the causal chain, evidence, contributing conditions, repair, and unresolved uncertainty.
families.boundary: Do not label a suspected cause as confirmed without discriminating evidence.

families.title: Separate types of uncertainty
families.method: Distinguish missing knowledge, natural variability, measurement error, and model uncertainty.
families.boundary: Different uncertainty sources require different remedies.

families.title: Use bounded estimates
families.method: Report a plausible interval or range when a point estimate would imply unjustified precision.
families.boundary: State how the bounds were obtained and what they do not cover.

families.title: Compare plausible scenarios
families.method: Evaluate the decision under a small set of materially different plausible conditions.
families.boundary: Do not present selected scenarios as exhaustive forecasts.

families.title: Test assumption sensitivity
families.method: Change important assumptions one at a time and observe whether the conclusion changes.
families.boundary: One-at-a-time tests can miss interactions between assumptions.

families.title: Use a robust satisficing threshold
families.method: Choose a solution that remains acceptable across the required range of conditions.
families.boundary: A robust solution may sacrifice peak performance; state the trade-off.

families.title: Track confidence by claim
families.method: Assign confidence separately to each material claim and explain the evidence basis.
families.boundary: Do not transfer confidence from one well-supported claim to adjacent claims.

families.title: Maintain an uncertainty register
families.method: List unresolved quantities, their potential impact, and the next way to reduce them.
families.boundary: Do not let the register become a substitute for resolving high-impact unknowns.

families.title: Check tail consequences
families.method: Examine low-probability outcomes whose consequences would be severe.
families.boundary: Do not imply that rare means impossible or quantify tails without data.

families.title: Use a conservative fallback
families.method: Define an action that remains safe when critical information is unavailable.
families.boundary: The fallback should not be described as optimal when it is only protective.

families.title: Separate confidence from importance
families.method: Assess how strongly a claim is supported and how much the decision depends on it.
families.boundary: A low-confidence claim may be unimportant; a high-impact claim may need further verification.

families.title: Use a value-of-information check
families.method: Estimate whether obtaining more information could change the choice enough to justify its cost.
families.boundary: Do not collect information indefinitely when it cannot alter the decision.

families.title: Record forecast calibration data
families.method: Store predictions and outcomes in a form that permits later comparison.
families.boundary: Do not evaluate calibration using only memorable or selectively retained forecasts.

families.title: Consider model disagreement
families.method: Compare outputs from genuinely different models and inspect why they diverge.
families.boundary: Do not average outputs when models use incompatible assumptions or scales.

families.title: Use uncertainty-aware language
families.method: Match wording to the strength and scope of the evidence.
families.boundary: Avoid numerical probabilities unless there is a defensible basis for them.

families.title: Identify robust conclusions
families.method: Find which conclusions remain unchanged across plausible assumptions or models.
families.boundary: Do not call a conclusion robust if the tested range is narrow or arbitrary.

families.title: Set an uncertainty acceptance limit
families.method: Specify which unknowns are tolerable before action and which require escalation.
families.boundary: The limit must reflect consequence severity and authority.

families.title: Avoid false precision
families.method: Round outputs to a precision justified by input quality and method.
families.boundary: Do not discard meaningful variation merely to make a result look neat.

families.title: Update estimates transparently
families.method: When new information arrives, record which estimate changed and why.
families.boundary: Do not overwrite earlier estimates when auditability matters.

families.title: Distinguish possibility from likelihood
families.method: State whether a scenario is merely conceivable or supported as reasonably likely.
families.boundary: A vivid possible event is not thereby probable.

families.title: State conditions for abstention
families.method: Define which missing evidence or failed checks make a conclusion unsafe to provide.
families.boundary: Abstention should identify what would resolve the limitation when possible.

families.title: Budget effort by task uncertainty
families.method: Spend more investigative effort where uncertainty can materially change the outcome.
families.boundary: Do not spend high effort on details that cannot affect the decision.

families.title: Protect critical resources
families.method: Reserve scarce resources for tasks that are prerequisites to the objective.
families.boundary: Do not reserve capacity without a defined use or release condition.

families.title: Account for coordination overhead
families.method: Include communication, integration, review, and handoff effort in resource estimates.
families.boundary: Do not assume parallel work reduces elapsed time when coordination is the bottleneck.

families.title: Prefer low-cost information first
families.method: Use safe inexpensive checks before expensive investigations when they can discriminate between options.
families.boundary: Do not let cheap but weak checks replace necessary high-assurance evidence.

families.title: Use a resource reserve
families.method: Set aside capacity for predictable variance and recovery.
families.boundary: A reserve is not free capacity for unplanned scope expansion.

families.title: Measure marginal benefit
families.method: Compare the expected improvement from the next unit of effort with its cost.
families.boundary: Do not assume the next unit has the same benefit as earlier units.

families.title: Avoid premature optimization
families.method: Resolve the dominant requirement before tuning secondary performance details.
families.boundary: Do not defer a known structural flaw under the label of later optimization.

families.title: Reduce switching overhead
families.method: Group related work to reduce repeated setup and context changes.
families.boundary: Batching must not delay time-critical results.

families.title: Use graceful degradation
families.method: Define how service or solution quality should reduce when resources become scarce.
families.boundary: Degraded operation must remain within safety and correctness constraints.

families.title: Match tool to task scale
families.method: Choose a tool whose capacity and precision fit the size and consequence of the task.
families.boundary: A sophisticated tool can add error when its assumptions are misunderstood.

families.title: Track resource consumption
families.method: Measure actual time, compute, materials, and attention used by major activities.
families.boundary: Do not infer future cost from one atypical run.

families.title: Separate fixed from variable cost
families.method: Identify costs that remain regardless of volume and costs that change with use.
families.boundary: Check the relevant time horizon before classifying a cost as fixed.

families.title: Include maintenance burden
families.method: Estimate the ongoing effort required to keep a chosen solution usable.
families.boundary: Initial build cost alone is not total cost of ownership.

families.title: Use the smallest sufficient experiment
families.method: Choose the smallest trial that can safely answer the decision question.
families.boundary: Do not under-size the trial when rare failure or subgroup effects matter.

families.title: Prioritize irreversible resource use
families.method: Review commitments that permanently consume capacity before optional spending.
families.boundary: Do not delay essential investment merely because it is irreversible.

families.title: Set a scope-change budget
families.method: Define how much additional work can be accepted without renegotiating the objective.
families.boundary: A scope budget does not authorize changes that violate safety or contract constraints.

families.title: Compare buy, build, reuse, and defer
families.method: Evaluate materially different acquisition paths using the same lifetime criteria.
families.boundary: Do not assume reuse is free or external procurement is always faster.

families.title: Identify resource substitution limits
families.method: Record which resources can replace one another and which cannot.
families.boundary: Do not treat unlike skills, materials, or compute resources as interchangeable.

families.title: Plan for resource contention
families.method: Identify activities that compete for the same constrained resource.
families.boundary: A schedule is infeasible when shared resource demand exceeds capacity.

families.title: Release unused reservations
families.method: Return capacity to the shared pool when a dependency or task no longer needs it.
families.boundary: Confirm that the reservation is genuinely unnecessary before release.

families.title: Map source and target roles
families.method: Identify which entities and relationships correspond between an analogy source and target.
families.boundary: Do not map by surface resemblance alone.

families.title: Transfer structure before detail
families.method: Carry over the relationship pattern while re-deriving target-specific values.
families.boundary: A source example does not establish target-specific facts.

families.title: List disanalogies explicitly
families.method: Record features that differ and may break a proposed transfer.
families.boundary: A single decisive disanalogy can invalidate the analogy for the intended use.

families.title: Identify invariant relationships
families.method: Find the structure that remains stable under changes in names, units, or representation.
families.boundary: Do not claim invariance without checking the allowed transformations.

families.title: Use a counter-domain test
families.method: Try the proposed principle in a context where its assumptions may fail.
families.boundary: A failed transfer narrows scope rather than necessarily refuting the source principle.

families.title: Translate examples into schemas
families.method: Extract roles, constraints, and relations from a concrete case.
families.boundary: Do not preserve incidental details as if they were essential.

families.title: Use analogy to generate a test
families.method: Derive a candidate prediction from the source structure and test it directly in the target.
families.boundary: Treat the prediction as a hypothesis until tested.

families.title: Separate metaphor from mechanism
families.method: Label figurative comparisons and state what concrete mechanism, if any, they represent.
families.boundary: Do not use a metaphor as evidence.

families.title: Compare abstraction levels
families.method: Check that source and target are described at compatible levels before transfer.
families.boundary: A micro-level mechanism may not predict a macro-level outcome.

families.title: Re-derive units and scales
families.method: Recompute quantitative relationships using target units and scales.
families.boundary: Never copy a source numerical value solely because the analogy is close.

families.title: Transfer only tested invariants
families.method: Use a cross-domain principle only after its key assumptions are checked in the new setting.
families.boundary: Do not generalize from one successful transfer to every domain.

families.title: Use contrasting analogies
families.method: Compare multiple analogies that illuminate different aspects of the target.
families.boundary: Do not let one analogy hide features that another exposes.

families.title: Create a boundary example
families.method: Construct a target case near the limit of the analogy's assumptions.
families.boundary: A boundary example is a probe, not a full validation.

families.title: Identify role reversals
families.method: Check whether source and target roles preserve direction and responsibility.
families.boundary: A reversed role can reverse the meaning of the relationship.

families.title: Abstract the shared constraint
families.method: Find the constraint that makes two different problems structurally similar.
families.boundary: Shared vocabulary alone is not structural similarity.

families.title: Separate reusable method from domain facts
families.method: Transfer a reasoning procedure while sourcing domain-specific premises independently.
families.boundary: A valid method cannot compensate for false target facts.

families.title: Record transfer confidence
families.method: State which parts are structurally matched and which remain speculative.
families.boundary: Do not turn a plausible analogy into an asserted equivalence.

families.title: Test a negative analogy
families.method: Identify a superficially similar case where the principle should not apply.
families.boundary: Use the negative case to mark the boundary, not as an irrelevant exception.

families.title: Translate constraints across representations
families.method: Map each source constraint into an equivalent target condition before applying the method.
families.boundary: If no faithful mapping exists, do not claim direct transfer.

families.title: Extract a reusable pattern
families.method: Replace domain-specific labels with roles and operations that preserve the essential structure.
families.boundary: The abstraction must retain conditions that make the pattern valid.

families.title: Run an independent consistency pass
families.method: Re-read the result using a separate checklist focused on contradictions and omissions.
families.boundary: A repeated review using the same assumptions may repeat the same error.

families.title: Check claims against their definitions
families.method: Verify that each key term is used consistently with the definition chosen for the task.
families.boundary: Do not change a definition mid-argument to preserve a result.

families.title: Inspect edge conditions
families.method: Test limiting, empty, extreme, and transition cases relevant to the claim.
families.boundary: An edge case must satisfy the problem's stated preconditions to count as a refutation.

families.title: Check input-output alignment
families.method: Confirm that every output field or conclusion corresponds to a requested input or operation.
families.boundary: Do not add plausible but unrequested conclusions.

families.title: Verify units and dimensions
families.method: Check that combined quantities have compatible units and that outputs have expected dimensions.
families.boundary: Dimensional consistency is necessary but does not prove a numerical result is correct.

families.title: Perform a reverse audit trail
families.method: Start from the final conclusion and trace each step back to its evidence or assumption.
families.boundary: A traceable chain can still contain an invalid inference.

families.title: Check completeness against the objective
families.method: Compare the final result with every acceptance criterion stated at the start.
families.boundary: Do not declare completion based only on the easiest criteria.

families.title: Look for hidden scope changes
families.method: Compare the original question with the one actually answered.
families.boundary: A narrower answer is acceptable only when the limitation is made explicit.

families.title: Use a second representation
families.method: Re-express the result as a table, diagram, narrative, or independent calculation where useful.
families.boundary: Different representations may share the same underlying faulty assumptions.

families.title: Audit copied and transformed data
families.method: Check whether transformations changed ordering, units, labels, precision, or missing-value meaning.
families.boundary: A clean-looking output does not prove the transformation preserved meaning.

families.title: Check rounding and aggregation effects
families.method: Compare the aggregate result with underlying values and assess information lost.
families.boundary: Rounding errors can accumulate or reverse close comparisons.

families.title: Test contradiction handling
families.method: Introduce incompatible inputs and verify that the system flags rather than silently merges them.
families.boundary: Do not resolve a contradiction by arbitrarily preferring the latest record.

families.title: Verify exception paths
families.method: Check how the procedure behaves when a required input is absent or invalid.
families.boundary: A documented exception is not handled until the runtime or workflow enforces it.

families.title: Audit result reproducibility
families.method: Record the inputs, procedure version, settings, and environment needed to repeat the result.
families.boundary: Reproducibility does not guarantee correctness.

families.title: Use a failure-first review
families.method: Ask how the proposed result could be wrong and identify the cheapest discriminating check.
families.boundary: Do not manufacture remote objections that cannot affect the decision.

families.title: Check for duplicated counting
families.method: Trace whether the same event, cost, benefit, or source appears in multiple parts of the result.
families.boundary: Duplicates can remain hidden when labels differ.

families.title: Check sign and direction conventions
families.method: Confirm the meaning of positive, negative, increase, decrease, and direction labels.
families.boundary: Do not assume conventions are shared across sources.

families.title: Check temporal ordering
families.method: Ensure events and evidence are placed in an order compatible with the proposed process.
families.boundary: Timestamp precision and clock alignment may limit ordering claims.

families.title: Validate the final artifact against its schema
families.method: Check required fields, data types, identifiers, and allowed values before use.
families.boundary: Schema validity does not establish semantic validity.

families.title: Keep a correction record
families.method: Record what changed, why it changed, and which previous result is superseded.
families.boundary: Do not erase audit history when correcting a result.

families.title: State the answer before supporting detail
families.method: Lead with the decision or conclusion, then present the reasons needed to evaluate it.
families.boundary: Do not state a decisive answer first when key uncertainty makes it misleading.

families.title: Make the reasoning chain inspectable
families.method: Show the important intermediate steps between evidence and conclusion.
families.boundary: Do not expose irrelevant internal detail that obscures the argument.

families.title: Label fact, inference, and recommendation
families.method: Mark direct evidence, derived interpretation, and value-based advice distinctly.
families.boundary: A recommendation may combine facts and values; identify both.

families.title: Attach qualifications to the relevant claim
families.method: Place scope limits and uncertainty beside the statement they qualify.
families.boundary: A distant disclaimer may not prevent a local overstatement.

families.title: Use a claim-reason-evidence structure
families.method: State a claim, the reason connecting evidence to it, and the evidence itself.
families.boundary: A reason without evidence or an evidence list without inference is incomplete.

families.title: Explain technical terms on first use
families.method: Define specialized language when the intended audience may not know it.
families.boundary: Do not replace a precise term with an inaccurate simplification.

families.title: Separate disagreement types
families.method: Identify whether parties disagree about facts, definitions, methods, values, or priorities.
families.boundary: Resolving one type does not automatically resolve another.

families.title: Use a comparison table for multiple options
families.method: Choose dimensions first, then describe each option using the same structure.
families.boundary: Tables should not conceal incomparable measurements or missing values.

families.title: Preserve source attribution
families.method: Name the origin of material claims and distinguish quotation from paraphrase.
families.boundary: Do not imply that a source endorses an inference it does not make.

families.title: Summarize without changing emphasis
families.method: Retain the source's central claim, evidence, uncertainty, and material caveats.
families.boundary: Do not promote a minor example into the source's main conclusion.

families.title: Write a decision-ready recommendation
families.method: State the recommended action, rationale, trade-offs, confidence, and review trigger.
families.boundary: Do not omit alternatives when the decision-maker needs a genuine choice.

families.title: Use an explicit unknowns section
families.method: List unresolved information that could change the answer.
families.boundary: Do not bury critical unknowns in generic caveats.

families.title: Use precise quantifiers
families.method: Choose terms such as all, most, some, or at least one to match the evidence.
families.boundary: Avoid universal language when only sampled cases were observed.

families.title: Distinguish disagreement from contradiction
families.method: Check whether two claims concern the same object, time, definition, and scope.
families.boundary: Different scopes can explain apparent disagreement without either claim being false.

families.title: Adapt detail to audience needs
families.method: Include the minimum background needed for the audience to assess or act on the result.
families.boundary: Do not remove critical assumptions merely to shorten the explanation.

families.title: Use examples to clarify boundaries
families.method: Pair a representative case with a nearby non-example when confusion is likely.
families.boundary: Do not let an illustrative example substitute for the rule itself.

families.title: Preserve uncertainty in summaries
families.method: Retain uncertainty that materially affects interpretation or action.
families.boundary: Do not convert tentative findings into definitive headlines.

families.title: Separate evidence from rhetoric
families.method: Remove persuasive wording that does not add a testable reason.
families.boundary: Neutral wording should not erase legitimate value differences.

families.title: End with an actionable next step
families.method: Identify the next check, decision, or action required to make progress.
families.boundary: Do not imply that an unperformed next step has already occurred.

families.title: Make disagreement auditable
families.method: Record each position and the evidence or assumption on which it depends.
families.boundary: Do not summarize a minority view so weakly that it becomes a straw position.

families.title: Elicit independent initial estimates
families.method: Ask contributors to record an initial view before group discussion when anchoring is a risk.
families.boundary: Independent estimates are not useful when contributors lack the relevant information or skill.

families.title: Assign distinct review roles
families.method: Separate evidence gathering, method checking, implementation review, and decision authority.
families.boundary: Do not let role separation prevent essential cross-checking.

families.title: Use a shared evidence ledger
families.method: Give collaborators a common record of claims, sources, dates, and unresolved issues.
families.boundary: A shared ledger requires ownership and update rules.

families.title: Record dissenting views
families.method: Capture material minority interpretations and the reasons supporting them.
families.boundary: Do not equate consensus with correctness.

families.title: Clarify decision rights
families.method: State who recommends, who approves, and who is accountable for implementation.
families.boundary: Do not confuse consultation with veto authority.

families.title: Normalize terminology across teams
families.method: Agree on working definitions for terms that cross team boundaries.
families.boundary: Preserve domain-specific meanings when one shared definition would be misleading.

families.title: Separate coordination from evaluation
families.method: First clarify what each contributor did; then independently assess the quality of the result.
families.boundary: Do not mistake activity reporting for evidence of effectiveness.

families.title: Use structured challenge
families.method: Ask a reviewer to identify the strongest failure case for the preferred proposal.
families.boundary: Challenge should target assumptions and evidence, not the person.

families.title: Rotate critical review
families.method: Assign reviewers to examine different assumptions or components over time.
families.boundary: Rotation is useful only when reviewers have enough context and competence.

families.title: Make handoff state explicit
families.method: Transfer current status, artifacts, pending decisions, and known limitations.
families.boundary: A handoff is incomplete when assumptions remain only in the previous owner's memory.

families.title: Resolve interface ownership
families.method: Assign responsibility for information and outputs shared between groups.
families.boundary: Unowned interfaces create gaps even when each team completes its local task.

families.title: Distinguish consensus from unanimity
families.method: Record whether a decision is unanimous, majority-supported, or authorized despite dissent.
families.boundary: Do not represent an authorized decision as unanimous agreement.

families.title: Use asynchronous review windows
families.method: Give contributors a fixed period and clear questions for independent review.
families.boundary: Time-boxing must not replace urgent safety escalation.

families.title: Reconcile duplicate work
families.method: Compare parallel outputs and identify shared evidence before merging conclusions.
families.boundary: Do not combine duplicated evidence as independent confirmation.

families.title: Preserve provenance across handoffs
families.method: Keep source references and transformation history when transferring data or analysis.
families.boundary: Do not detach a claim from its limitations during summarization.

families.title: Use a common issue taxonomy
families.method: Classify open problems consistently so owners can compare and prioritize them.
families.boundary: Do not force unique issues into categories that distort their meaning.

families.title: Escalate unresolved authority conflicts
families.method: Identify the rule or role needed to resolve competing instructions.
families.boundary: Do not invent authority when governance is unclear.

families.title: Protect independent review
families.method: Prevent the author of a result from being its only reviewer when stakes are high.
families.boundary: Independence needs access to inputs and method, not just a different name.

families.title: Close the feedback loop with contributors
families.method: Tell contributors which issues were accepted, rejected, or left open and why.
families.boundary: Do not imply that feedback was incorporated when no change was made.

families.title: Maintain a decision log
families.method: Record what was decided, by whom, when, and on which evidence and assumptions.
families.boundary: A decision log records governance; it does not make the decision correct.

families.title: Select a reasoning mode before acting
families.method: Choose whether the task calls for exploration, estimation, diagnosis, comparison, or formal checking.
families.boundary: Switch modes when the evidence or task changes.

families.title: Estimate the consequence of error
families.method: Classify the downside of a wrong answer before deciding how much verification is needed.
families.boundary: Do not use low stakes as a reason to fabricate missing facts.

families.title: Set a stopping condition
families.method: Define what evidence or result is sufficient to stop the current search.
families.boundary: Reopen the search if a new material contradiction appears.

families.title: Monitor method effectiveness
families.method: Check whether the current approach is reducing uncertainty or making measurable progress.
families.boundary: Do not continue a method solely because effort has already been invested.

families.title: Detect unproductive repetition
families.method: Notice when repeated steps produce no new information or change in state.
families.boundary: Repeat when independent replication is the goal.

families.title: Escalate when competence is insufficient
families.method: Identify when specialized knowledge, authority, or tools are required beyond current capability.
families.boundary: Do not use escalation to avoid ordinary checks that can be completed safely.

families.title: Choose tools by decision relevance
families.method: Select a tool only when its output can inform a stated subgoal or test.
families.boundary: Tool availability is not a reason to use it.

families.title: Preserve working context
families.method: Record current goal, assumptions, completed checks, and next action before pausing.
families.boundary: Do not store unnecessary personal or sensitive material.

families.title: Audit confidence after new evidence
families.method: Revisit confidence when a new observation materially changes the evidence base.
families.boundary: Do not change confidence merely to match a preferred conclusion.

families.title: Separate familiarity from competence
families.method: Check whether the task has actually been performed successfully rather than merely recognized.
families.boundary: Prior exposure is not proof of present capability.

families.title: Identify motivated reasoning risk
families.method: Ask what evidence would make the preferred conclusion less credible.
families.boundary: Do not assume disagreement is motivated simply because it challenges a view.

families.title: Use a pre-mortem
families.method: Imagine the plan failed and list plausible failure causes before commitment.
families.boundary: Treat the list as risk discovery, not a prediction that all failures will occur.

families.title: Use a post-mortem
families.method: After completion or failure, compare expectations with events and identify changeable causes.
families.boundary: Avoid hindsight certainty and blame without causal evidence.

families.title: Separate confidence from fluency
families.method: Check whether an answer is supported rather than relying on how easily it was produced.
families.boundary: A difficult explanation is not automatically more accurate.

families.title: Protect time for verification
families.method: Reserve time to inspect the result before delivery or irreversible action.
families.boundary: Do not let verification become an unlimited second project.

families.title: Define escalation thresholds
families.method: Specify conditions that require human review, specialist input, or a halt.
families.boundary: Thresholds should reflect consequence and legal or safety obligations.

families.title: Track unresolved questions
families.method: Keep an explicit list of questions that remain open after the current pass.
families.boundary: Do not present unresolved questions as settled merely because the task is closing.

families.title: Change method after a failed test
families.method: Diagnose why the current approach failed before selecting a materially different method.
families.boundary: Do not randomly switch methods without preserving the failure evidence.

families.title: Avoid sunk-cost continuation
families.method: Evaluate the next action using future costs and benefits rather than effort already spent.
families.boundary: Past investment may still matter if it creates a real transferable asset.

families.title: Review the final answer from the user's goal
families.method: Check whether the result actually answers the requested question or advances the stated objective.
families.boundary: Do not optimize presentation at the expense of task completion.

families.title: Identify system stocks and flows
families.method: Separate accumulated quantities from rates that change those quantities.
families.boundary: Do not infer a flow directly from one stock measurement.

families.title: Map feedback polarity
families.method: Record whether a feedback loop amplifies or counteracts a change.
families.boundary: A loop's overall effect may depend on delay and operating conditions.

families.title: Account for time delays
families.method: Identify lags between action, intermediate effects, and measured outcomes.
families.boundary: Do not interpret an early measurement as the final system response.

families.title: Find system bottlenecks
families.method: Identify the constrained stage that limits overall throughput or performance.
families.boundary: Local capacity increases may not improve the system if the bottleneck is elsewhere.

families.title: Check for displacement effects
families.method: Ask whether an improvement in one area shifts cost or load to another.
families.boundary: Do not claim a net improvement without checking the system boundary.

families.title: Inspect coupled components
families.method: Identify components whose behavior changes when another component changes.
families.boundary: Independent component tests may miss coupled failure.

families.title: Consider emergent behavior
families.method: Check whether interactions create system-level behavior not present in any component alone.
families.boundary: Do not invoke emergence as an explanation without identifying interactions.

families.title: Track cumulative effects
families.method: Assess whether small repeated changes accumulate over the relevant horizon.
families.boundary: Do not extrapolate linear accumulation when saturation or thresholds may occur.

families.title: Check threshold behavior
families.method: Identify points where gradual input changes trigger a discontinuous response.
families.boundary: Do not assume smooth proportional behavior around a threshold.

families.title: Assess resilience to component loss
families.method: Determine whether the system can maintain essential functions after a component fails.
families.boundary: Redundancy is ineffective when backups share the same failure mode.

families.title: Map external feedback
families.method: Identify how users, markets, institutions, or environments respond to system outputs.
families.boundary: External actors may adapt, making past behavior a poor guide to future response.

families.title: Inspect second-order effects
families.method: Trace how the first consequence changes conditions that produce later consequences.
families.boundary: Do not extend a causal chain indefinitely without evidence or a useful stopping point.

families.title: Separate local from global optimization
families.method: Check whether a locally optimal action worsens whole-system performance.
families.boundary: Use the actual system objective, not a proxy chosen by one component.

families.title: Identify common-cause failures
families.method: Look for shared conditions that can disable multiple supposedly independent components.
families.boundary: Do not count correlated backups as independent resilience.

families.title: Assess path dependence
families.method: Check whether the sequence of earlier states changes which future states are reachable.
families.boundary: Do not assume a reset is possible when prior actions leave persistent effects.

families.title: Locate irreversible state changes
families.method: Identify transitions that cannot be cheaply or fully undone.
families.boundary: Treat irreversible changes with stronger pre-commitment checks.

families.title: Model adaptation by other actors
families.method: Consider how people or components may change behavior in response to a rule or incentive.
families.boundary: Do not assume behavior remains fixed after the intervention.

families.title: Track interactions between objectives
families.method: Identify where improving one objective worsens another.
families.boundary: Do not collapse competing objectives without an explicit priority rule.

families.title: Use system boundary stress tests
families.method: Test what happens when external inputs, demand, or environment approach boundary conditions.
families.boundary: A boundary stress test does not estimate normal operating frequency.

families.title: Reassess after structural change
families.method: Rebuild the model when components, relationships, or incentives materially change.
families.boundary: Do not continue using a model whose structure no longer matches the system.

contexts.trigger_condition: the requested outcome has more than one plausible interpretation
contexts.adjustment: state the competing interpretations and avoid choosing silently; use the interpretation that is explicitly supported or request the missing decision
contexts.guard: do not treat an inferred preference as an instruction
contexts.example_hint: a request to make a process better without defining better

contexts.trigger_condition: one or more required inputs are absent
contexts.adjustment: mark each missing input and determine whether it is blocking, estimable, or safely defaultable
contexts.guard: never invent a missing value that materially changes the result
contexts.example_hint: a plan request omits its budget and deadline

contexts.trigger_condition: observations contain measurement noise or inconsistent readings
contexts.adjustment: preserve raw readings, characterize the noise source, and avoid overreacting to a single deviation
contexts.guard: do not remove outliers without a documented reason
contexts.example_hint: several measurements vary around an expected operating range

contexts.trigger_condition: credible reports disagree about the same event or state
contexts.adjustment: align time, scope, definitions, and source lineage before deciding whether the reports truly conflict
contexts.guard: do not count copied reports as independent evidence
contexts.example_hint: two teams report different completion states for one task

contexts.trigger_condition: only a small number of relevant observations are available
contexts.adjustment: narrow the conclusion to what the observed cases support and identify the most informative next check
contexts.guard: do not generalize frequency or prevalence from a tiny selected sample
contexts.example_hint: a new process has only been tried twice

contexts.trigger_condition: the decision must be made under a short deadline
contexts.adjustment: prioritize checks that can change the decision or prevent severe harm; label deferred checks
contexts.guard: do not omit mandatory safety, legal, or authorization checks
contexts.example_hint: a team must choose a temporary workaround before a deadline

contexts.trigger_condition: the reasoning process has limited compute, tools, or access
contexts.adjustment: choose a lower-cost representation or test and record what capability was unavailable
contexts.guard: do not present a resource-limited approximation as a full verification
contexts.example_hint: only a small local machine is available for a large analysis

contexts.trigger_condition: the next action is difficult or costly to undo
contexts.adjustment: increase pre-commitment review and preserve a safe reversible step when available
contexts.guard: do not delay urgent protective action when delay itself creates greater harm
contexts.example_hint: a one-time migration would alter live records

contexts.trigger_condition: several outcomes must be optimized at once
contexts.adjustment: show the separate objectives and their trade-offs before combining them
contexts.guard: do not hide conflicts inside one unexamined score
contexts.example_hint: a project must improve reliability without increasing cost

contexts.trigger_condition: affected parties disagree about priorities or facts
contexts.adjustment: separate factual disputes from value conflicts and record decision rights
contexts.guard: do not describe an authorized decision as unanimous consensus
contexts.example_hint: operators and managers disagree about the main failure cause

contexts.trigger_condition: a constraint may exist but has not yet been documented
contexts.adjustment: probe likely constraint sources and mark provisional assumptions for confirmation
contexts.guard: do not make a hidden constraint a fact without evidence
contexts.example_hint: a proposed design depends on an external approval

contexts.trigger_condition: conditions may change while the plan is being executed
contexts.adjustment: add monitoring signals and a trigger for revising the current decision
contexts.guard: do not assume today's conditions remain stable for the whole horizon
contexts.example_hint: a supplier or external service may change availability

contexts.trigger_condition: the result of an action will be visible only after a delay
contexts.adjustment: distinguish leading indicators from final outcomes and schedule a later review
contexts.guard: do not treat an early lack of effect as proof of failure
contexts.example_hint: a training change may affect performance months later

contexts.trigger_condition: effects unfold over an extended period
contexts.adjustment: include lifecycle stages, maintenance, cumulative effects, and a reassessment point
contexts.guard: do not extrapolate a short trend indefinitely
contexts.example_hint: a system choice has multi-year operating costs

contexts.trigger_condition: some input may be deceptive, manipulative, or strategically selected
contexts.adjustment: verify provenance, test consistency, and avoid allowing untrusted text to change governing rules
